# Capabilities

A *capability* is a named operation with one implementation, reachable identically from
the CLI, the local HTTP daemon, an MCP host, the Web cockpit, and the VS Code extension
(ADR-004). The table below is generated from the registry, so it is exactly what this
build exposes. Regenerate with:

```bash
uv run python docs/guide/gen_capabilities.py
```

Print the same list from a workspace with `research capabilities` (add `--schemas` for
each capability's request and response JSON schema, or `--json` for the whole descriptor).

## Permissions

| permission | what it may touch |
|---|---|
| `read` | accepted state and the regenerable projection; writes nothing |
| `stage` | `.research/staging/` only — proposals a person still has to review |
| `mutate` | accepted scientific state |
| `admin` | rebuilds or initialises regenerable infrastructure |

Who holds them:

| principal | granted | how it is recognised |
|---|---|---|
| `human` | `read`, `stage`, `mutate`, `admin` | the CLI, and any caller with the daemon token |
| `agent_host` | `read`, `stage` | any MCP host, and an HTTP caller with no valid token |
| `model` | `read`, `stage` | an internal model worker (Product 21) |

`mutate` and `admin` additionally require a human principal whatever else was granted, so
an agent host that calls one gets `permission_denied` rather than a partial write. The
**human** column below marks capabilities that need the researcher; it is true for every
`mutate` and `admin` capability and for anything else flagged `human_only`.

## The table

**MCP tool** is the capability name with dots replaced by underscores, which is the whole
mapping — a host that has seen `claim.audit` in the catalog knows to call `claim_audit`.

| capability | MCP tool | permission | human | what it does, and what it changes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `anchor.list` | `anchor_list` | `read` |  | Every manuscript sentence bound to a Claim. reads canonical state; changes nothing. |
| `citation.verify` | `citation_verify` | `read` |  | Check every manuscript citation key against the bibliography. reports missing or unused citation keys; changes nothing. |
| `claim.audit` | `claim_audit` | `mutate` | yes | Record what the evidence allows a Claim to say. writes the Claim's assessment: status, allowed strength, defensible wording. |
| `claim.create` | `claim_create` | `mutate` | yes | Register a structured Claim. creates a Claim at its requested strength; the audit decides what it may say. |
| `claim.find_counterevidence` | `claim_find_counterevidence` | `read` |  | Retrieval proposals that might bear against a Claim. proposes places to look; creates no Evidence and no relation. |
| `claim.find_support` | `claim_find_support` | `read` |  | The evidence a Claim records, resolved, grouped by relation. reads claim-evidence relations; changes nothing. |
| `claim.list` | `claim_list` | `read` |  | Claim summaries, filtered by status, staleness, and type. reads canonical state; changes nothing. |
| `claim.override_strength` | `claim_override_strength` | `mutate` | yes | Apply an accepted epistemic override to a Claim. raises or lowers a Claim's allowed strength under a recorded Decision. |
| `claim.relate` | `claim_relate` | `mutate` | yes | Link one evidence object to a Claim under a relation and aspect. adds one claim-evidence edge; never rewrites the claim's assessment. |
| `claim.supersede` | `claim_supersede` | `mutate` | yes | Retire a Claim, optionally naming the claim that replaces it. moves a Claim to superseded, which is terminal; human-only. |
| `claim.unrelate` | `claim_unrelate` | `mutate` | yes | Remove exactly one claim-evidence edge. drops one claim-evidence edge; the assessment is left as it was. |
| `claim.update_coverage` | `claim_update_coverage` | `mutate` | yes | Record the search coverage a Claim's scope rests on. writes the deterministic discovery funnel onto a Claim; the audit reads it and no model contributes to it. |
| `corpus.ingest` | `corpus_ingest` | `mutate` | yes | Register a local file as an immutable Artifact of a Work. creates Work/Version/Artifact identity from a file; proposes no evidence. |
| `corpus.screen` | `corpus_screen` | `mutate` | yes | Include or exclude one discovery candidate, with its reason. records a screening decision on a SearchRun; acquires no source. |
| `corpus.search` | `corpus_search` | `mutate` | yes | Search the configured external sources and record the run. reads external catalogues and writes nothing to them; records the SearchRun that makes the operation reproducible, and adds nothing to the corpus. |
| `decision.accept` | `decision_accept` | `mutate` | yes | Accept a proposed researcher Decision. moves a Decision to accepted; a researcher act (Product 38). |
| `decision.list` | `decision_list` | `read` |  | Recorded researcher decisions, optionally for one Claim. reads canonical state; changes nothing. |
| `decision.supersede` | `decision_supersede` | `mutate` | yes | Retire an accepted Decision, optionally naming its replacement. moves a Decision to superseded; the record of the choice stays. |
| `evidence.accept` | `evidence_accept` | `mutate` | yes | Accept a reviewed candidate as canonical Evidence. creates accepted Evidence from a reviewed candidate; requires a human actor. |
| `evidence.extract` | `evidence_extract` | `stage` |  | Extract evidence for a Work's fields; the interrogation run, by field. stages evidence candidates under .research/staging; accepts nothing. Returns a run id. |
| `evidence.list` | `evidence_list` | `read` |  | Accepted evidence by work and status; staged proposals are not listed. reads canonical state; changes nothing. |
| `evidence.reject` | `evidence_reject` | `mutate` | yes | Refuse a candidate and record why. records a refusal so the same proposal is recognised again; creates no Evidence. |
| `evidence.verify` | `evidence_verify` | `stage` |  | Re-read the source for staged candidates; returns a run id. writes verification verdicts onto staged candidates; accepts nothing. Returns a run id. |
| `manuscript.anchors` | `manuscript_anchors` | `read` |  | Every stored anchor, with its verdict against the manuscript on disk. reads anchors and computes their verdicts; records none of them. |
| `manuscript.attach_claim` | `manuscript_attach_claim` | `mutate` | yes | Bind a manuscript sentence to a Claim. creates the manuscript anchor that makes a sentence auditable (Product 30.1). |
| `manuscript.audit` | `manuscript_audit` | `read` |  | Audit the manuscript against the accepted research graph. reports findings; repairs nothing and writes nothing. |
| `manuscript.draft` | `manuscript_draft` | `stage` |  | Draft a section from named accepted Claims, into staging. writes a draft candidate under .research/staging; the manuscript is untouched. |
| `manuscript.revalidate` | `manuscript_revalidate` | `mutate` | yes | Re-find every stored anchor and record what the manuscript now says. records anchor relocation and staleness; a reworded sentence goes stale rather than being reattached, and it requires a human actor. |
| `manuscript.trace` | `manuscript_trace` | `read` |  | One sentence, by file and line, down to its Claim and source spans. reads the traceability chain; changes nothing. |
| `note.add` | `note_add` | `mutate` | yes | Capture a low-authority research note. creates a note that can never be cited as support until it is promoted. |
| `note.discard` | `note_discard` | `mutate` | yes | Retire a captured note; discarded is terminal. ends a note's life; nothing downstream moves. |
| `note.promote` | `note_promote` | `mutate` | yes | Record the research object a captured note became. raises a note's authority into a Claim, Question, or Decision; human-only. |
| `question.create` | `question_create` | `mutate` | yes | Register a research question. creates an open ResearchQuestion; answers nothing. |
| `question.list` | `question_list` | `read` |  | Research questions and what currently bears on them. reads canonical state; changes nothing. |
| `question.resolve` | `question_resolve` | `mutate` | yes | Answer a research question and capture the answer as a note. moves a ResearchQuestion to answered; writes no evidence. |
| `question.update` | `question_update` | `mutate` | yes | Move a question's status and relink what bears on it. changes a ResearchQuestion's status and links; writes no evidence. |
| `retrieval.resolve_source` | `retrieval_resolve_source` | `read` |  | Reopen a reference at its exact source location. reads a source anchor; changes nothing. |
| `retrieval.search` | `retrieval_search` | `read` |  | Search the corpus and accepted state, accepted state first. reads the deletable indexes; changes nothing. |
| `review.accept` | `review_accept` | `mutate` | yes | Accept one staged candidate, named by its staging id. creates accepted Evidence from a staged candidate and marks the candidate reviewed; requires a human actor. |
| `review.accept_batch` | `review_accept_batch` | `mutate` | yes | Accept every candidate meeting the Product 24.4 batch conditions. creates accepted Evidence for candidates meeting deterministic conditions; requires a human actor and a permitting policy. |
| `review.candidate` | `review_candidate` | `read` |  | One staged candidate, verbatim, as a review action posts it back. reads a staged proposal; accepts nothing and changes nothing. |
| `review.defer` | `review_defer` | `stage` | yes | Put one candidate aside; it stays in the queue. records the researcher's note on a staged candidate; accepts nothing. |
| `review.edit` | `review_edit` | `mutate` | yes | Accept the researcher's corrected Evidence for one candidate. creates accepted Evidence from corrected content; the source anchor may never move, and it requires a human actor. |
| `review.inbox` | `review_inbox` | `read` |  | The review queue, in Product 24.2 priority order. reads staged candidates and their conflicts; accepts nothing. |
| `review.qualify` | `review_qualify` | `mutate` | yes | Accept one candidate with the condition it holds under. creates accepted Evidence carrying a qualification; requires a human actor. |
| `review.reject` | `review_reject` | `mutate` | yes | Refuse one candidate, with the reason recorded beside the corpus. records a refusal so the same proposal is recognised again; creates no Evidence and requires a human actor. |
| `review.request_more` | `review_request_more` | `stage` | yes | Ask for more evidence; the question is captured as a durable note. records the request on the staged candidate and captures it as a low-authority note; accepts nothing. |
| `review.resolve_conflict` | `review_resolve_conflict` | `mutate` | yes | Resolve a conflicting proposal the researcher's way. accepts, rejects, or defers one candidate; the reason is recorded. |
| `review.split` | `review_split` | `mutate` | yes | Accept the source fact and deal with its interpretation separately. creates exactly one accepted Evidence for the source half of a candidate and stages or refuses the interpretation half; requires a human actor. |
| `run.cancel` | `run_cancel` | `stage` |  | Ask a running workflow to stop before its next stage. sets a durable cancel flag on regenerable run state. |
| `run.status` | `run_status` | `read` |  | The durable record of one long-running workflow run. reads regenerable run state; changes nothing. |
| `search_run.get` | `search_run_get` | `read` |  | One discovery run with its candidates and the metadata they propose. reads a recorded SearchRun and derives the metadata its candidates offer; proposes nothing to the corpus and changes nothing. |
| `search_run.list` | `search_run_list` | `read` |  | Recorded discovery runs with their funnel counts, newest first. reads canonical state; changes nothing. |
| `search_run.record` | `search_run_record` | `mutate` | yes | Persist a reproducible discovery operation. records what was searched, where, and when; adds nothing to the corpus. |
| `state.index` | `state_index` | `read` |  | Every navigation list - works, claims, questions, decisions - in one read. reads canonical state; changes nothing. |
| `state.rebuild` | `state_rebuild` | `admin` | yes | Rebuild the deletable projection from canonical files. rebuilds regenerable state only; canonical files are never written. |
| `state.stale` | `state_stale` | `read` |  | What is out of date, highest scientific impact first. reads recorded stale marks; recomputes and rewrites nothing. |
| `synthesis.build_matrix` | `synthesis_build_matrix` | `mutate` | yes | Persist a cross-paper comparison matrix. writes a synthesis matrix over accepted evidence; proposes no new facts. |
| `synthesis.compare` | `synthesis_compare` | `read` |  | One field across the corpus, as a comparison table. reads an existing synthesis matrix; proposes no classification. |
| `taxonomy.put` | `taxonomy_put` | `mutate` | yes | Write a taxonomy authorised by an accepted Decision. replaces a classification vocabulary; downstream classifications go stale. |
| `work.add_artifact` | `work_add_artifact` | `mutate` | yes | Attach a new immutable file to an existing Work. adds an Artifact (and a Version when needed); never overwrites one. |
| `work.get` | `work_get` | `read` |  | Read one Work with its versions, artifacts, and derived counts. reads corpus state; changes nothing. |
| `work.interrogate` | `work_interrogate` | `stage` |  | Ask a Work the interrogation schema's questions; returns a run id. stages evidence candidates under .research/staging; accepts nothing. Returns a run id. |
| `work.list` | `work_list` | `read` |  | Every Work in the corpus, with its files and evidence counts. reads canonical state; changes nothing. |
| `work.parse` | `work_parse` | `mutate` | yes | Parse a Work's artifact into structural blocks and store them. stores a derived parse so anchors resolve; changes no evidence. |
| `work.register` | `work_register` | `mutate` | yes | Register a resolved candidate as a Work, Version, and Artifact. creates corpus identity from a resolved candidate; writes no evidence. |
| `work.store_blocks` | `work_store_blocks` | `mutate` | yes | Persist a parse so anchors resolve without re-parsing. stores derived document blocks; changes no evidence or claim. |
| `work.update_metadata` | `work_update_metadata` | `mutate` | yes | Fill a Work's empty or undecodable bibliographic fields, with provenance. fills missing corpus metadata and records every disagreement; a decodable existing value is never overwritten unless the researcher asks. |

## Not built yet

These names exist in the product design but have no implementation in this build. Asking
for one returns "not built yet" rather than a stub that answers something plausible.

* `project.init` — creating a workspace is an admin action on an arbitrary filesystem path; the daemon is bound to one existing workspace, so it stays a CLI capability
* `synthesis.find_pattern` — no pattern-finding service exists yet (Phase 14)
